newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris seeks French firm based on Air Liberte - paper.
newsitem.headline: Paris seeks French firm based on Air Liberte - paper.

text.p: The French government wants to create an airline by bringing together privately-owned Euralair and AOM and buying up the insolvent Air Liberte, to keep out British Airways Plc, newspaper Le Monde reported on Friday.

The French move would thwart a potential purchase by BA of Air Liberte, which went into legal administration on September 26. BA earlier said its French TAT affiliate was in touch with the administrators to assess the assets. If BA were to buy Air Liberte, it would stand to gain valuable slots at Paris Orly airport.
But if Air Liberte, AOM and Euralair got together they would make a second force beside flagcarrier Air France.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), the holding company charged with selling Credit Lyonnais assets under a state-backed rescue plan.

The report said AOM chairman Alexandre Couvelaire would buy 51 percent of AOM, along with other investors, from CDR, to allow the airline to bid for Air Liberte. That is necessary as CDR was set up to sell assets, not buy them.
The AOM and Air Liberte merged company would then buy Euralair, the report said.

To avoid conflicts of interest -- Euralair owns 10 percent of Air Liberte -- Couvelaire has sold his 33 percent in Euralair to Ernest-Antoine Seilliere, chairman of French holding company CGIP, who is also a Euralair shareholder and board member, it said.
That 33 percent stake would be temporarily parked with Seilliere as it would be sold to the company formed out of Air Liberte and AOM.
Le Monde wrote that Seilliere formally denied the report but added that the French DGAC civil aviation authority confirmed the proposal. The DGAC registers changes in airline ownership.
If BA bought Air Liberte it would not merge it with TAT. It does not plan redundancies but would not renew 800 temporary contracts while keeping on the 1,300 permanent staff, the report said.
